component.name: Ferrous
component.summary: Play, browse and inspect your music library

description.p: Ferrous is a music player for KDE Plasma, made for listening closely. It aims to feel at home next to Dolphin and Kate, to stay quick however large your library grows, and to let you look into the music as well as listen to it.

ul.li: Gapless playback, with a queue that comes back where you left it
A spectrogram inspired by Adobe Audition's spectral view, a zoomable waveform and fullscreen viewers
A folder-first library that follows your folders as files change, with ranked search as you type
A tag editor for many files at once, with renames from tags that you see before anything changes
Full-size album art from the iTunes catalog, to preview and compare with yours before applying it
Last.fm scrobbling, MPRIS media controls and media keys

description.p: Which formats play depends on the installed GStreamer plugins.

description.p: A redesign: every part of the app was reworked in two rounds of design review, from the main window, the transport and its waveform seek bar to the spectrogram and waveform, menus, search, dialogs and the fullscreen viewers, with new motion and a new app icon.

ul.li: Change any keyboard shortcut, and redo an undone queue change
Drag or autoscroll the spectrogram and waveform to any part of the track, with the zoomed view marked on the seek bar
See the time under the pointer on the seek bar, and Last.fm's scrobble progress in the status bar
Many fixes, including safer tag editing and smoother playback across track changes
Ferrous now needs Qt 6.8 or newer
